_comment: One TTFV receipt per reader per track. Fill by hand following docs/measurement/ttfv-protocol.md; delete no keys. Null means not reached, not applicable, or unknown. Save as docs/measurement/receipts/YYYY-MM-DD-<handle>-<track>.json. track: demo | own-agent. date: YYYY-MM-DD of the attempt. facilitator: a handle only, no personal data. network: yes | no, whether the machine had internet access during the attempt; required yes for Track A and for uv tool install; checked once before the clock starts (protocol 2.7). coaching_events: list of {"at", "what"}. failures: list of {"at", "milestone", "what"}, kept even when the attempt failed.

reader._comment: handle: a public handle, no other personal data. kind: cold | maintainer | ai-agent; only cold receipts without coaching events count toward cold-reader metrics.

machine._comment: os and cpu as reported by the system (e.g. uname -sr, CPU model and core count); python and uv are `python3 --version` and `uv --version`. uv_cache: cold (fresh UV_CACHE_DIR) or warm.

package._comment: version: the agent-reliability-ci version installed. source: pypi or wheel. wheel_sha256: required when source is wheel (record UV_FIND_LINKS and any UV_CACHE_DIR in notes, protocol 2.3). readme_url: the README read, at a fixed commit.

project._comment: Track B only; null for demo. kind: own | sample. description: what the agent is, or which recipe the sample tree came from. refs_preexisting: baseline, candidate, toolset and oracle were importable before the clock started. workers: worker count of the run.

timestamps._comment: ISO 8601 with timezone, e.g. 2026-10-20T09:15:02Z. Track A uses readme_opened, command_start, demo_banner, demo_verdict, all_steps_held, interpretation_answered. Track B uses readme_opened, install_start, install_done, scaffold_start, descriptor_written, run_start, verdict_printed, store_validated, interpretation_answered. Leave the others null.

durations_seconds._comment: Whole seconds derived from the timestamps as the protocol defines per track (sections 3 and 4). agent_execution is Track B only: the sum of usage.wall_seconds over trials.jsonl in the run store (protocol 4.2), never subtracted from total.

outcome._comment: completed: every stop condition of the track held. verdict: PASS | BLOCK | INCONCLUSIVE | ERROR; Track B: the verdict stamped as verdict_printed; ERROR if none; Track A: the verdict for agent B. store_validated, decision_sha256, init_attempts, descriptor_hand_edited, trials_started: Track B only (protocol 4.3 and 4.6). descriptor_hand_edited: arci.yaml edited by hand before the run that produced the verdict, or, with no valid verdict, before any arci run that started trials. trials_started: trials.jsonl in the run store (protocol 4.2) exists and is non-empty. interpretation_correct is scored with the key in protocol 5.3.
outcome.verdict: BLOCK (exit 1) [A vs agent_b]; A 192/200 vs agent_b 132/200, matches the recorded run. Also A vs agent_a PASS (exit 0), A vs agent_c PASS (exit 0). Exit code note: in the first run my wrapper printed an empty 'exit:' because this shell is zsh (PIPESTATUS is bash-only), so I re-ran the identical command under bash (log: demo-rerun.log in the same dir; started 2026-10-13T12:15:10Z, All six steps held 2026-10-13T12:16:25Z) and it printed 'exit: 0'. All timestamps above are from the first run.
outcome.interpretation_answer: In the seeded demo, agent B (agent A with the retry around reserve removed) was worse than agent A under the injected reserve timeout by more than the allowed margin: 132/200 vs 192/200, with the upper bound of the difference below -0.10. So the gate says B should not ship (exit 1); it is a deliberate, expected result for the story, not a failure of the tool.

comprehension._comment: Answered once per reader, on the first track's receipt; on a second-track receipt set answered_on to that file name and leave the rest empty. Answers verbatim; scores per the key in protocol section 5; scorer is not the reader and is a handle only, no personal data. q2_who_for keeps its name for schema stability; it holds the whole q2 answer (who it is for and what the agent must expose).

answers.q1_what_is_it: ARCI (agent-reliability-ci) is a CLI/CI gate that runs a baseline agent and a candidate agent many times on the same predeclared tasks and injected tool faults, grades each run with an independent oracle, and returns PASS, BLOCK, INCONCLUSIVE or ERROR with an exit code (0/1/2/3). It can also diff, minimise and replay a recorded failure offline.
answers.q2_who_for: Someone who changes an agent (prompt, retry policy, refactor) and wants to know in CI whether the change made it less reliable. For a Python agent, they must expose four importable references: a baseline and a candidate function agent(task, tools, rng)->dict that call tools.call(...), a toolset factory (task, seed)->object with .tools and .snapshot(), and an oracle (task, final_state)->bool. Any program that speaks MCP over stdio can also be a command agent.
answers.q3_pass_means: For this predeclared experiment (its tasks, faults, N, alpha, delta), the evidence supports that any drop in success rate from baseline to candidate is smaller than the allowed margin delta (lower confidence bound on the difference is above -delta). It is relative non-inferiority only, not a claim of absolute reliability.
answers.q4_does_not_do: It is not a sandbox or security boundary (it assumes buggy but non-hostile agent code). It only sees calls that cross its tool boundary, so files, network or subprocess use outside it are invisible. It also does not replay model inference (replay re-serves recorded boundary calls, usually INVALID for a live model), and a trace divergence shows where runs differ, not why.
answers.q5_first_three_commands: 1) uv tool install agent-reliability-ci  2) arci init checkout-retry --baseline app.v1:run --candidate app.v2:run --toolset tests.world:make_world --oracle tests.world:passed  3) arci run arci.yaml. (The README also gives the same three chained with && in one line. In practice, install was blocked here so I used uv venv + uv pip install, and init needed an extra --task '{"order_id": "order-7"}' on my second try.)

Scorer rationale: All answers contain every required element, so there are no false scores.

q1: The reader describes a baseline-versus-candidate comparison, repeated runs on the same predeclared tasks and injected tool faults, and a gate verdict that names PASS and BLOCK (plus INCONCLUSIVE and ERROR).

q2: The reader names people who change an agent and want to know in CI whether it got less reliable. They give the callable shapes agent(task, tools, rng) and an MCP-over-stdio command.

q3: The reader says the drop is smaller than delta, with the lower bound above -delta. They say it is relative to the baseline, holds for this predeclared experiment, and is not a claim of absolute reliability.

q4: The reader lists three README limits: not a sandbox or security boundary, sees only calls across the tool boundary, and no model-inference replay. They add that a divergence shows where runs differ, not why.

q5: The commands are in the right order: uv tool install agent-reliability-ci, then arci init with --baseline, --candidate, --toolset and --oracle, then arci run arci.yaml. The notes about install being blocked and an extra --task flag are experience reports, not wrong claims.

Interpretation of BLOCK (demo): The reader says B is worse than A by more than the allowed margin under the injected reserve timeout, in the seeded demo. That matches the key's BLOCK reading, bounded to these conditions and this experiment.

Interpretation of the reader's own run (INCONCLUSIVE, exit 2): The reader says there is not enough evidence either way, no regression is claimed and no pass is granted. That matches the key.

failures.what: Not an arci error: my copy of the README-style wrapper printed 'exit: ' with an empty value because the Bash tool's shell is zsh and PIPESTATUS is a bash variable. Time is the end of the demo (All six steps held was logged 12:15:03Z); I re-ran the demo under bash at 2026-10-13T12:15:10Z and got 'exit: 0'.
